prompt: Name one of the twelve gifts in 'The Twelve Days of Christmas'.
label: Getting Harder
source: Frederic Austin's 1909 arrangement, which fixed the modern English text and the 'five gold rings' melody.
valueLogic: The partridge and the gold rings are near-universal. The middle band is the birds. The human gifts - maids, pipers, ladies, lords - are where people falter, and they get confused with each other, so they carry the highest values.
note: 'Birds' is deliberately not an alias of the calling birds: five gifts are birds, so the bare word gets a non-busting nudge to be specific instead of crediting one of them.

answers.name: A partridge in a pear tree
answers.fact: The first gift, and the only one that comes with its own tree.

answers.name: Five gold rings
answers.fact: The fifth, and the line everyone slows down for.

answers.name: Two turtle doves
answers.fact: The second. Turtle doves were a long-standing symbol of faithful love.

answers.name: Three French hens
answers.fact: The third gift, and the third bird in a row.

answers.name: Twelve drummers drumming
answers.fact: The twelfth and final gift, and the line the song builds to.

answers.name: Four calling birds
answers.fact: Originally colly birds - colly meaning black, so blackbirds.

answers.name: Seven swans a-swimming
answers.fact: The seventh, and by some reckonings the most expensive gift in the song.

answers.name: Ten lords a-leaping
answers.fact: The tenth, and the gift most often swapped with the ladies by mistake.

answers.name: Six geese a-laying
answers.fact: The sixth. Some argue the gold rings were ring-necked birds, which would make six birds in a row.

answers.name: Nine ladies dancing
answers.fact: The ninth, and frequently confused with the leaping lords.

answers.name: Eleven pipers piping
answers.fact: The eleventh, and the one most often misremembered as drummers.

answers.name: Eight maids a-milking
answers.fact: The eighth, and the single hardest of the twelve to recall unprompted.

distractors.name: Thirteen
distractors.note: There is no thirteenth gift - the song has twelve.

distractors.name: Lords a-dancing
distractors.note: A blend of two gifts. The lords leap and the ladies dance.

distractors.name: Birds
distractors.note: Five of the gifts are birds - say which one.
